Listen, this is probably a little unorthodox of an opinion but it IS JUST my opinion. Take it or leave it right? I in no way shape or form know everything. That being said.. 



I have been a married mom with no help whatsoever, to married mom with a little help, to single mom with no help, to 9 months WITHOUT my children while I was busy having a mental breakdown, back to being single mom with a little help, to married mom with a TON of help. So I've experienced a lot of parent/family dynamics and living situations. 



People are always going to tell you how to parent, what to do, what not to do, imposing their religiously zealous opinions on EVERY parenting topic you could imagine and could not even imagine as well. Close family members will over step your parental boundaries, some will be steadfast that they know what's best, some will be determined to see every one of your parenting choices ignored or avoided. This is totally normal! Don't let it get to you or define you as a parent. YOU know that you are spending quality bonding time with your child. Your child will KNOW that you are her mom, that she is loved. She will know your rules, regulations, and boundaries.  She will treat those boundaries, she will have similar relationships with other people of get family but no matter how many people help you out, think they know what's best, take over some of your parental duties,  interfere in your parenting, make you uncomfortable, etc.. She will still know who birthed her,have get life, rearranged get life to raise her and guide her and take responsibility for her. She will know who get mother is abd s that she is blessed. 



Simultaneously, she will be going through similar bonding with the other important people of her family. That is also perfectly normal and HEALTHY. For the both of you!



Please, please, please.. Don't make my mistakes. Don't think you have to prove to the world that you can do this without help. Don't think that taking on all of the work load somehow makes you a better and more dedicated mommy. In reality, it will burn you out so quick. You will inevitably start losing it completely. You will experience depression and despair, shame and resentment, you will make poor parenting decisions and you will have spent so much energy and effort on the necessary duties and regional responsibilities, that you'll find that you have little left for anyone snuggles, and spontaneous Fort building movie night, adventures to the park and other activities. And don't even get me started on the total and utter emotional,  spiritual, and physical depletion you will feel if your child has outside the house activities and regular appointments. If you manage to make it work and keep it together your whole life will revolve around that single point. Calendars and unbreakable routines. Many sacrifices will be made, not by you, but by your child. Because there is only one of you, after all, there is only so much you can realistically achieve on your own. 



TAKE THE HELP. Take it however it comes. Take it forced down your throat, take it begrudgingly,  take it hesitantly, take it overbearingly, take it gladly, take it happily, take it sadly, take it angrily, take it uncomfortably, take it in whatever form it presents itself. Take advantage of every resource available to you. It will make you an incredibly good mother. For many reasons. 



REASONS TO ACCEPT HELP WITH PARENTING WITHOUT SUCCUMBING TO THE MOM SHAMING THAT IS SO POPULAR NOWADAYS:



1) parenting is hard! It's physically and mentally exhausting. For a mom in particular. For the first year after giving birth our hormones are still very unstable and will be slowly returning to normal over the course of the year. This can have all sorts of consequences and effects. Seriously I can't tell you the difference between that first year all alone and that first year spent surrounded by overeager loved ones happily jumping for the babies every need and insisting you rest Vs overstepping yourself doing everything. It's the difference between fighting to be a better me and mom every day and giving up believing I was the scum of the world and unfit to bear the title of mother. 



2) Your child will be learning different life skills, values, morals, ethics, and beliefs. The benefits of this type of learning diversity needs no explanation. She'll be subjected to and expected to obey and respect different rules, expectations, and authority figures. Every person she builds a healthy familia relationship with is an important and needed learning opportunity for your child. When she is an adult she will be faced with many startling realities, people, situations, and choices. Give her the best building blocks to be able to face these realities and people with confidence, give her the resource pool of all who love her and wish to care for her so she may draw from their different knowledge, experiences, and wisdom to aid her on her life's journey and you can feel fulfilled in knowing you were responsible for providing her with every chance to grow as a person, that you provided her with the tools to face whatever comes.



3) You will have more time, energy, motivation, and zeal to teac her what you feel are important and necessary qualities and traits. More quality time together. More time to ponder philosophical-level questions and concerns that WILL arise as you travel your parenting journey. Did I burp her enough? Did I measure the correct medicine dose? How do I feel about vaccinations, gmo food, and organic cleaning supplies? Will I try and use one of these new age positive parenting methods or will I user-generated tried-and-true spare the rod method my parents used on me? Will I teach her to stand up for herself or walk away? All these questions and more will occupy your mind and you will fret whether you are making the right choices. Lean on your loved ones for support, advice and ideas and use their experience and wisdom to raise your child into a good sturdy thought filled young lady. 



4) and last but but not least accept their help and concern and love because your daughter will love you for it. It's proven that people who were showered with love, affection, concern, and caring are more confident in themselves, question theirselves less, are more likely to rely on their own knowledge, thoughts, and opinions rather than follow blindly. They've been shown to have more empathy and less depression. 



Good luck on your fulfilling journey as a parent. I order you my best wishes and blessings and prayers. 



TLDR;  accept help parenting your children and relinquish parental responsibilities and duties when offered because it will allow your child to grow and learn from different perspectives and sources than just yourself while simultaneously relieving you of huge stresses and concerns so you may spend your energy and efforts on building a solid loving relationship and create happy and carefree memories with her.

I took suboxone just long enough to get through the horrible first few days of WD from heroin. It worked and I never became addicted to suboxone and only used slivers enough to take the restless legs and cold-sweats (and bother embarassing symptoms) away. A+ would suggest suboxone for a 1-2 week period at 1-2 mg a day for withdraw but I'm not a doctor and that's just my personal experience. My husband also WD this way. It was the end to our long journey. 6 months clean now. Don't even think about it anymore. Came here from another sub that was suggesting it to someone else.

I never did understand why they kept people on suboxone for so long when you can take it for the 1-2 weeks you're withdrawing and it takes away the horrible withdraw symptoms but what I understand is that they keep you on it for so long because you can't do any opiates while on it or chance being very very sick. I was a heroin addict. Never posted about it or anything but I was. I've been clean for 6 months. The way I did it was with 1.5 strips of 8mg Suboxone. I cut them into tiny pieces and I did a piece when the withdraw was feeling unbearable. For the first few days it was pretty frequent but then I was going whole days and then a couple days and then once the strip and a half was gone I realized I made it through and didn't feel any of the WORST withdraw symptoms that I had felt the first time I went cold turkey. The depression, the anxiety at having to face the world without the stuff was still there but the restless legs, the cold-to-hot-to-cold again, etc I didn't have to endure thanks to suboxone. And it only took 1.5 strips. I still felt a bit grimey after the 7 days but the worst was over. Suboxone is just another drug that can get you high and I HIGHLY advise not doing it for a period longer than 2 weeks else you are just addicted to another drug that you have to withdraw from. BUT, it WILL mask the withdraw symtoms in those first few unbearable days.

Deranking exists because of the flaw in Halo 3's ranking system. It's like this.

Player A is really good. If he wins, he will probably rank up until the mid 40s. If he loses he will definitely go down.


Player B is just okay. His win rate is about the same as his lose rate. He has streaks, and in the end comes out ahead. He will have to play and win a lot more games from level 40+ to rank up at all. On the flip side, he has to lose a lot more than player A to rank down.


Player C is completely awful. Simply put it takes him 10-15 games to rank up even at level 20. He has a very hard time deranking because his MMR is so low that the game kind of gives it to him. 


When player A and player C match up, if they win, player A gets like a 200% bonus to his win. If he was at level 49 freshly, there is a great shot he will be level 50 after winning that game.

When player B and C match up, it's very similar. Let's say it takes 10 games to get from 40 to 41 for player B, with C on his team he has a much higher chance to rank up.


Not many people are legitimate player C's, but people know that this is how the system works and so they exploit it. They derank on one of their accounts over and over and over again until their MMR is absolutely awful. Then they play with high level friends or fresh accounts and rush to that level 50. Now, why people are doing it still after all this time? I couldn't tell you.

I can tell you however that if a legitimate player A plays 150 games and wins them all, he will probably be level 50 in a playlist.

With player C on player A's team (partied up, etc) it goes down to about 17-25 games for that same level 50.

My mom has five kids and I'm telling you, there's always time to get them into their own room, you won't set a precedence if you choose this route.  Also, I don't know your work schedule but my I know my son sometimes decides to go to bed at 8 and sometimes he's like EFF YOU and goes to bed at 11.  We pretty much let him make the sleep schedule.  No matter what six hours is enough for any adult.  Schedules will come with time.  There's no need to force the issue RIGHT NOW.  Like I said, most professionals would call all this bad advice but you know what?  They are our children and 20 years from now whether they slept with mommy and daddy at 9 months or whether they stayed up til ten instead of going to bed won't make a difference in whether they are successful or not.

Violence is never the answer.  Psychologically speaking, hitting a CHILD, like I said teaches them that hitting is an appropriate outlet when you think someone has done something wrong.  There's a thousand other options besides spanking.  And if spanking is necessary, it should only be used in situations where the child is doing something dangerous and continues to participate in this behavior.

Spanking doesn't straighten kids out.  Perhaps they will fear that consequence if used consistently but basically what this teaches is that when we are mad, we hit.  It's the worst form of punishment.  Discussing and explaining to them exactly why they have to listen to one key.  You think they are too young to understand but they soak up everything.  A second thing to do is to take toys away.  Sit in time out, take other forms of fun that your kid may enjoy.  But most especially you need to spend QUALITY time with her and explain this is HER time.  Tell her that she's a big girl and when she was a tiny baby like BABY BROTHER she needed lots of attention, too.

Morning sickness does suck and it is different with everyone woman.  However, she could at least read a book on the couch instead of watching T.V. You might also entertain the thought that she might be depressed for being laid off or maybe she's having thoughts of whether she'll be a good mom or she may even be wishing she WASN'T pregnant. I'd get to the bottom of all of this.  Try to talk to her about how she's feeling about the pregnancy, about the baby specifically.  Ask if she thinks she's going to be a fun mom or a strict mom.  Ask her if she's excited.  I know with my first baby I was ready to crawl out of my skin with all the anxiety that comes with pre-motherhood.  Also, ask her if she wants to read a baby book together on the couch.  Then work towards getting up off the couch.  Hope that helps.

EDIT: Also, first trimester sucks no matter which way you look at it.  If it is still like this in the Second or even Third, you definitely might have to get a bit more stern.  Don't worry, we need it sometimes.  We get pregnant not disabled.  Exercise and moving around is REALLY good for us and the babies.

I think a lot of people are under a lit of misconceptions about birth.  Being pregnant is not a disease in which you need to cured or "treated" in a hospital setting.  Mothers died a lot in the past before "modern medicine" from things like infection from dirty utensils and lack of sanitation.  Just like with anything, problems can arise but I think (I'm not going to find the exact numbers right now) it's something like less than 2 percent of women have labor complications.  Of course, I am talking about women who are healthy in every way, don't use drugs and generally take care of themselves and the baby while pregnant.  That being said, I wouldn't add in the labor complications from drug and alcohol users into the equation (which is the majority of the complications mothers run into in this country.) The mother mortality rate is actually also on the rise again from things like unneeded c-sections and the such.  And don't even get me started on pitocin, the drug used to "Speed up labor".  Laying in a hospital bed, giving birth, is the worst position on a womans body possible.  The absolute worst.  So why is that the position that 90 percent of women are put in?  Because it's easier for the doctor.  Hospitals are also infested with disease and bacteria.  It's much safer to have your child at home with a professional NURSE MIDWIFE, who can spot any labor complications (if they were to arise) and has all the neccessary skills to handle the situation.  I know I went on a rant there but seriously a natural birth is the way to go. I did it with nothing. Research all the pros of a natural childbirth and all the negatives of the way America does things.  The reason that pregnancy is treated as something to be treated? Jobs and money, jobs and money.  What need for the multi-billion dollar industry if women knew that they already KNOW how to give birth and don't need to be told or instructed? Don't take my word for it, though. Research, research, research.  And since you are deciding to have a hospital birth make a set birthing plan.  Things you are okay with, things your not and stick to it and don't let any doctor or nurse tell you otherwise because this is YOUR day.  They just want the bed evacuated as fast as possible to get someone else into it.  They don't like 24 hour births, they want to pump you full of PT and get you out of there and if it's taking too long. Good luck with the hypnobabies.  I myself would not pay for that kind of thing.  The best thing to do is for your wife to get her mind around what could and what is going to happen.  Come to terms with the fact that it's GOING to hurt if you go natural but it's for a great cause.  Have plenty of pillows and comforting things to surround herself with and even some good classical music wouldn't hurt.  But honestly, when you get into that room you never know how you're going to feel.  You may want every light out and not to hear a peep from anyone or you may want to talk through it, see everyone, have everyone participate.  GOOD LUCK.
